extractions.description: The paper introduces SynFlowNet, a GFlowNet model whose action space is defined by chemical reactions and purchasable building blocks, for generating synthesizable molecules. It compares against fragment-based GFlowNets, REINVENT, SyntheMol, SynNet and soft Q-learning, studies backward policy training schemes (maximum likelihood, REINFORCE), scaling of the building block action space with Morgan fingerprints, and target-specific building block curation using experimental fragment screens.
